LESSON: READING 3.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry, part of Strand 3 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do people write poems? 2. What makes a poem interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the structure of poems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the structure of varied simple poems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. read short poems addressing varied societal issues,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the poem’s structure in communicating a message.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the structure of poems,

   Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse the structure of varied simple poems,

   Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. read short poems addressing varied societal issues,

   Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the poem’s structure in communicating a message.

   Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. source online or offline for different poems and note the titles and the poets while observing integrity and cyber safety,

2. brainstorm on the parts of a poem,

3. read short poems addressing issues such as personal hygiene, HIV and AIDS, and COVID-19,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. source online or offline for different poems and note the titles and the poets while observing integrity and cyber safety,
2. brainstorm on the parts of a poem,
3. read short poems addressing issues such as personal hygiene, HIV and AIDS, and COVID-19,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: It is achieved as the learner uses digital devices to search sources online for different poems and notes the titles

and the poets, while observing cyber safety.

Values:
Integrity is achieved as the learner searches online or offline for poems while observing cyber security.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Health Education is promoted as the learner tackles poems on issues such as personal hygiene, HIVand AIDS, and

COVID-19

• Cyber Safety is promoted as the learner searches online or offline for poems.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the structure of poems to other learning areas such as Kiswahili and Creative Arts and Sports.

2. analyse the structure of varied simple poems,
